# Be lazy. Do more. Go fast. _Flux is a reactive UI library for Luau. It's strictly typed for accurate autocomplete, batches updates once per frame, and keeps syntax terse enough to read like plain Luau._ [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/kohltastrophe/flux/ci.yml?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/kohltastrophe/flux/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kohltastrophe/flux/badges/coverage.json&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/kohltastrophe/flux/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/kohltastrophe/flux?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE.md) [![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kohltastrophe/flux?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/kohltastrophe/flux/releases) ---
Flux leans on Luau's type checker so your editor does the heavy lifting. When you declare a `TextLabel` or `Frame`, you get autocomplete for every valid property, event, and expected type. ---
```luau local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Flux = require(ReplicatedStorage.Flux) local new = Flux.new local count = Flux(0) new "ScreenGui" { Parent = playerGui, new "TextButton" { Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50), Text = function() return `Clicks: {count}` end, Activated = function() count(count + 1) end, }, } ``` Every reactive node supports `__call` and operator overloading, so reading and writing state takes no extra ceremony. Call `count()`

--!strict
--[[
Async resources: a fetcher runs off the graph, and its progress is exposed as nodes (`data`, `error`, `loading`,
`state`). A race guard keeps only the latest fetch's result.

```luau
local profile = Flux.async(userId, function(id) return fetchProfile(id) end)
```
]]

local Compat = require("./Compat")
local Graph = require("./Graph")

local effect = Graph.effect
local raw = Graph.raw
local read = Graph.read
local signal = Graph.signal
local untrack = Graph.untrack
local retrack = Graph.retrack
local task = Compat.task

local function gatedOff(src: any, input: any): boolean
	return src ~= nil and (input == nil or input == false)
end

--[[
The state of an [async](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async) node, derived from its `.error`/`.loading` and whether a fetch has resolved.
- `unresolved` (nothing fetched yet)
- `pending` (first fetch in flight, no value)
- `refreshing` (fetch in flight over an existing value)
- `ready` (resolved)
- `errored` (last fetch threw)
]]
export type AsyncState = "unresolved" | "pending" | "ready" | "refreshing" | "errored"

-- An async resource: its progress as nodes, and `refetch`, `mutate` and `Destroy`.
export type Async<T> = {
	data: Graph.Node<T?>,
	error: Graph.Node<string?>,
	loading: Graph.Node<boolean>,
	state: Graph.Node<AsyncState>,
	--[[
	Destroys the async node, cleaning up all resources.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
	]]
	Destroy: (self: any) -> (),
	--[[
	Re-runs the fetcher with the current source value without writing the source node.
	An optional `refetching` payload is forwarded to the fetcher (defaults to `true`).

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
	]]
	refetch: (self: any, refetching: any?) -> (),
	--[[
	Optimistically writes `data` and invalidates any in-flight fetch.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
	]]
	mutate: (self: any, value: T) -> (),
}

--- @ignore
type Data = {
	data: Graph.Node<any>,
	error: Graph.Node<string?>,
	loading: Graph.Node<boolean>,
	state: Graph.Node<AsyncState>,
	_resolved: boolean,
	_effect: Graph.Node<any>,
	_src: any,
	_fetcher: any,
	_fetchId: number,
}

local function runFetcher(self: Data, input: any, currentId: number, refetching: any)
	local ok, result = pcall(self._fetcher, input, raw(self.data), refetching)
	if currentId ~= self._fetchId then
		return
	end
	self.loading:set(false)
	if ok then
		self._resolved = true
		self.data:set(result)
		self.state:set("ready")
	else
		self.error:set(tostring(result))
		self.state:set("errored")
	end
end

local function trigger(self: Data, input: any, refetching: any)
	self._fetchId += 1
	local currentId = self._fetchId
	self.loading:set(true)
	self.error:set(nil)
	self.state:set(if self._resolved then "refreshing" else "pending")
	untrack()
	task.spawn(runFetcher, self, input, currentId, refetching)
	retrack()
end

local Async = {}
Async.__index = Async

local function new(source: any, fetcher: any, initialValue: any): Async<any>
	local src: any = source
	local fetch: any = fetcher
	local init: any = initialValue
	if type(fetch) ~= "function" then
		src, fetch, init = nil, source, fetcher
	end

	local self: any = setmetatable({
		data = signal(init),
		error = signal(nil :: string?),
		loading = signal(false),
		state = signal("unresolved" :: AsyncState),
		_resolved = false,
		_effect = nil,
		_src = src,
		_fetcher = fetch,
		_fetchId = 0,
	}, Async)

	self._effect = effect(function()
		local input = read(src)
		if gatedOff(src, input) then
			self._fetchId += 1
			self.loading:set(false)
			self.error:set(nil)
			self.state:set(if self._resolved then "ready" else "unresolved")
			return
		end
		trigger(self, input, false)
	end)

	if Graph.getOwner() then
		Graph.cleanup(self)
	end

	return self
end

--[[
Destroys the async node, cleaning up all resources.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
]]
function Async.Destroy(self: Data)
	if self._effect == nil then
		return
	end
	self.state:Destroy()
	self.data:Destroy()
	self.error:Destroy()
	self.loading:Destroy()
	self._effect:Destroy()
	local nextId = self._fetchId + 1
	local rawSelf: any = self
	table.clear(rawSelf)
	self._fetchId = nextId
end

--[[
Optimistically writes `data` and invalidates any in-flight fetch.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
]]
function Async.mutate(self: Data, value: any)
	if self._effect == nil then
		return
	end
	self._fetchId += 1
	self._resolved = true
	self.loading:set(false)
	self.error:set(nil)
	self.data:set(value)
	self.state:set("ready")
end

--[[
Re-runs the fetcher with the current source value without writing the source node.
An optional `refetching` payload is forwarded to the fetcher (defaults to `true`).

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async)
]]
function Async.refetch(self: Data, refetching: any?)
	if self._effect == nil then
		return
	end
	local src = self._src
	local input = raw(src)
	if gatedOff(src, input) then
		return
	end
	trigger(self, input, if refetching == nil then true else refetching)
end

--[[
Runs yielding work off the reactive graph and exposes its progress as `.data`, `.error`, `.loading`, and `.state` nodes.
`fetcher(value, previous, refetching)` runs untracked whenever `source` is truthy, and stale in-flight results are discarded automatically.

```luau
local profile = Flux.async(userId, function(id) return Players:GetNameFromUserIdAsync(id) end)
Flux.new "TextLabel" { Text = function() return profile.data() or "Loading" end }
```

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/async#creating-an-async-node)
]]
Async.new = new :: (<S, T>(
	source: S,
	fetcher: (value: Graph.Unwrap<S>, previous: T?, refetching: any) -> T,
	initialValue: T?
) -> Async<T>) & (<T>(fetcher: (value: nil, previous: T?, refetching: any) -> T, initialValue: T?) -> Async<T>)

return table.freeze(Async)

--!strict
local Compat = require("./Compat")
local Graph = require("./Graph")
local Type = require("./Type")

local compatTask = Compat.task
local compatTypeof = Compat.typeof
local warn = Compat.warn

local effect = Graph.effect
local get = Graph.Node.get
local kindOf = Graph.kindOf
local new = Graph.new
local signal = Graph.signal
local raw = Graph.raw
local read = Graph.read
local untrack = Graph.untrack
local isNode = Graph.isNode
local isReactive = Graph.isReactive
local withOwner = Graph.withOwner

local MODEL_SYMBOL: any = table.freeze({ type = "Model" })
local NO_VALUE: any = nil
local NOOP = function() end

--- @ignore
type BindData = {
	fn: { [(value: any) -> ()]: boolean },
	rbx: { [Instance]: { { [string]: any }? } },
	eff: Graph.Node<any>,
	flushed: boolean,
	children: {
		cleanupConnection: RBXScriptConnection?,
		list: { Instance },
		parent: Instance?,
		order: number?,
		token: number?,
	}?,
}

local bindData: { [Graph.Node<any>]: BindData } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local bindGeneration = 0

-- The source that currently drives each instance property or attribute (attributes keyed with a `$` prefix). An edit
-- that sets the key again, bound or static, releases the previous claim first, so the newest value wins and stays
-- instead of racing the original source whenever it changes. A claim is a list of releasers: its unbind, then anything
-- edit attached to it (the node it made from a function, a model's read-back connection).
type Claim = { (() -> ()) | Graph.Node<any> }
local claims: { [Instance]: { [string]: Claim } } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

local function claimKey(property: string, isAttribute: boolean?): string
	return if isAttribute then "$" .. property else property
end

local function release(instance: Instance, property: string, isAttribute: boolean?)
	local owned = claims[instance]
	if owned == nil then
		return
	end
	local key = claimKey(property, isAttribute)
	local claim = owned[key]
	if claim == nil then
		return
	end
	owned[key] = nil
	if next(owned) == nil then
		claims[instance] = nil
	end
	for _, releaser in claim do
		if type(releaser) == "function" then
			releaser()
		else
			Graph.dispose(releaser)
		end
	end
end
local pinnedOrder: { [Instance]: boolean } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

local function applyLayoutOrder(child: Instance, order: number): number
	if child:IsA("GuiObject") and (child :: GuiObject).LayoutOrder == 0 and not pinnedOrder[child] then
		(child :: GuiObject).LayoutOrder = order
		return order + 1
	end
	return order
end

local function isInstance(value: any): boolean
	return kindOf(value) == "Instance"
end

local function collectChildren(value: any, into: { Instance }): { Instance }
	if isInstance(value) then
		table.insert(into, value)
	elseif isNode(value) then
		collectChildren(get(value), into)
	elseif type(value) == "table" then
		for _, child in value do
			collectChildren(child, into)
		end
	end
	return into
end

local function applyChildren(bind: BindData, value: any)
	local data = bind.children
	if data == nil then
		return
	end
	local list = data.list
	local parent = data.parent
	local layoutOrder = data.order or 1

	while isNode(value) do
		value = get(value)
	end

	if type(value) == "table" and not isInstance(value) then
		local children = collectChildren(value, {})
		if list[1] ~= nil then
			if children[2] == nil then
				local first = children[1]
				for _, child in list do
					if child.Parent == parent and child ~= first then
						child.Parent = nil
					end
				end
			else
				local incoming: { [Instance]: true } = {}
				for _, child in children do
					incoming[child] = true
				end
				for _, child in list do
					if child.Parent == parent and incoming[child] == nil then
						child.Parent = nil
					end
				end
			end
			table.clear(list)
		end
		for count, child in children do
			layoutOrder = applyLayoutOrder(child, layoutOrder)
			list[count] = child
			child.Parent = parent
		end
	else
		for _, child in list do
			if child.Parent == parent and child ~= value then
				child.Parent = nil
			end
		end
		table.clear(list)
		if value ~= nil and isInstance(value) then
			local child = value :: Instance
			applyLayoutOrder(child, layoutOrder)
			list[1] = child
			child.Parent = parent
		end
	end
end

local function setAttribute(instance: Instance, attr: string, value: any)
	instance:SetAttribute(attr, value)
end

local function setProperty(instance: Instance, prop: string, value: any)
	local rawInstance: any = instance
	rawInstance[prop] = value
end

local function resolveKey(name: string, isAttribute: boolean?): (string, boolean, boolean)
	if isAttribute ~= nil then
		return name, isAttribute, false
	end
	local first = string.byte(name)
	if first == 36 then
		local attr = string.sub(name, 2)
		if attr == "" then
			error('attribute name after "$" cannot be empty', 4)
		end
		return attr, true, false
	elseif first == 35 then
		local tag = string.sub(name, 2)
		if tag == "" then
			error('tag name after "#" cannot be empty', 4)
		end
		return tag, false, true
	elseif first == 95 then
		if string.sub(name, 1, 6) == "_attr_" then
			local attr = string.sub(name, 7)
			if attr == "" then
				error('attribute name after "_attr_" cannot be empty', 4)
			end
			return attr, true, false
		elseif string.sub(name, 1, 5) == "_tag_" then
			local tag = string.sub(name, 6)
			if tag == "" then
				error('tag name after "_tag_" cannot be empty', 4)
			end
			return tag, false, true
		end
	end
	return name, false, false
end

local function onTagChanged(instance: Instance, tag: string, fn: (hasTag: boolean) -> ()): () -> ()
	local collectionService = Compat.getService("CollectionService")
	if collectionService == nil then
		return NOOP
	end
	local last = instance:HasTag(tag)
	local function check(inst: Instance)
		if inst == instance then
			local current = instance:HasTag(tag)
			if current ~= last then
				last = current
				fn(current)
			end
		end
	end
	local added = collectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag):Connect(check)
	local removed = collectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag):Connect(check)
	local ancestry = instance.AncestryChanged:Connect(function()
		check(instance)
	end)
	return function()
		added:Disconnect()
		removed:Disconnect()
		ancestry:Disconnect()
	end
end

local function onChanged(
	instance: Instance,
	name: string,
	isAttribute: boolean?,
	fn: (value: any) -> ()
): RBXScriptConnection
	if isAttribute then
		return instance:GetAttributeChangedSignal(name):Connect(function()
			fn(instance:GetAttribute(name))
		end)
	end
	local rawInstance: any = instance
	return instance:GetPropertyChangedSignal(name):Connect(function()
		fn(rawInstance[name])
	end)
end

local function writeInstance(bind: BindData, value: any)
	for instance, syncTo in bind.rbx do
		local attrs = syncTo[1]
		if attrs then
			for attr in attrs do
				setAttribute(instance, attr, value)
			end
		end
		local props = syncTo[2]
		if props then
			for prop in props do
				setProperty(instance, prop, value)
			end
		end
	end
end

local function writeBinds(bind: BindData, value: any)
	if next(bind.rbx) ~= nil and not pcall(writeInstance, bind, value) then
		for instance, syncTo in bind.rbx do
			local attrs = syncTo[1]
			if attrs then
				for attr in attrs do
					local ok, result = pcall(setAttribute, instance, attr, value)
					if not ok then
						warn(`[Flux] failed to set attribute "{attr}" of {instance:GetFullName()}: {result}`)
					end
				end
			end
			local props = syncTo[2]
			if props then
				for prop in props do
					local ok, result = pcall(setProperty, instance, prop, value)
					if not ok then
						warn(`[Flux] failed to set property "{prop}" of {instance:GetFullName()}: {result}`)
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

local function cleanupChildrenBind<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>, parent: Instance?)
	local data = bindData[node]
	local children = data and data.children
	if not children then
		return
	end
	if children.cleanupConnection then
		children.cleanupConnection:Disconnect()
	end
	for _, child in children.list do
		local current = child and child.Parent
		if current ~= nil and (parent == nil or current == parent) then
			child.Parent = nil
		end
	end
	table.clear(children.list)
	table.clear(children)
	data.children = nil
end

local function startBindEffect(node: Graph.Node<any>, data: any): Graph.Node<any>
	data.flushed = false
	-- Writing instance properties fires engine listeners (`Changed`, `GetPropertyChangedSignal`, `AncestryChanged`)
	-- synchronously. Run the writes untracked and ownerless so those listeners neither subscribe this effect to
	-- what they read nor hand it the instances they create (which it would destroy on its next run). Children
	-- stay tracked: nested child nodes are read while mounting them.
	local pending: any = nil
	local notifyListeners = false
	local function write()
		local value = pending
		local shouldNotify = notifyListeners
		pending = nil
		notifyListeners = false
		if shouldNotify then
			local fns = data.fn
			local first = next(fns)
			if first ~= nil then
				if next(fns, first) == nil then
					compatTask.spawn(first, value)
				else
					local list = table.create(4)
					for fn in fns do
						table.insert(list, fn)
					end
					for _, fn in list do
						if fns[fn] then
							compatTask.spawn(fn, value)
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
		writeBinds(data, value)
	end
	local function isolated()
		untrack(write)
	end
	local eff = withOwner(NO_VALUE, function()
		return effect(function()
			local notify = data.flushed
			data.flushed = true
			local value = get(node)
			local hasFn = notify and next(data.fn) ~= nil
			if hasFn or next(data.rbx) ~= nil then
				pending = value
				notifyListeners = hasFn
				withOwner(NO_VALUE, isolated)
			end
			applyChildren(data, value)
		end)
	end)
	return eff
end

local function getBindData<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>)
	local data: any = bindData[node]
	if data == nil then
		data = { fn = {}, rbx = {}, children = nil, eff = nil, flushed = false }
		bindData[node] = data
		data.eff = startBindEffect(node, data)
		node:onDestroy(function()
			data.eff:Destroy()
			table.clear(data.fn)
			table.clear(data.rbx)
			cleanupChildrenBind(node)
			bindData[node] = nil
		end)
	end
	return data
end

local function bindDestroy(node: Graph.Node<any>, disconnect: () -> ()): () -> ()
	local rawNode: any = node
	local done = false
	local function disconnectOnce()
		if done then
			return
		end
		done = true
		local inner = rawNode[1]
		local destroys = inner and inner.destroys
		if destroys then
			local idx = table.find(destroys, disconnectOnce)
			if idx then
				table.remove(destroys, idx)
			end
		end
		disconnect()
	end
	node:onDestroy(disconnectOnce)
	return disconnectOnce
end

local Bind = {
	--- @ignore
	pinOrder = function(instance: Instance)
		pinnedOrder[instance] = true
	end,
	--- @ignore
	applyLayoutOrder = applyLayoutOrder,
	--- @ignore
	setAttribute = setAttribute,
	--- @ignore
	setProperty = setProperty,
	--- @ignore
	onChanged = onChanged,
	--- @ignore
	onTagChanged = onTagChanged,
	--- @ignore
	bindDestroy = bindDestroy,
}

--[[
Wraps a reactive [node](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/signals) for two-way binding on an [`Instance`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance) property, attribute, or tag.
Updates the instance from `node` and writes changes back to `node` when the instance fires its changed signal.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/creation#flux-model-two-way-binding-in-one-key)
]]
function Bind.model<N>(node: N): Graph.Unwrap<N>
	if not isNode(node) then
		error("Flux.model expects a reactive node", 2)
	end
	local wrapped: any = table.freeze({ MODEL_SYMBOL, node })
	return wrapped
end

--[[
Returns `true` when `value` is a [`Flux.model`](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/creation#flux-model-two-way-binding-in-one-key) wrapper.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/creation#flux-model-two-way-binding-in-one-key)
]]
function Bind.isModel(value: unknown): boolean
	local rawValue: any = value
	return type(value) == "table" and rawValue[1] == MODEL_SYMBOL
end

--[[
Returns the underlying node from a [`Flux.model`](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/creation#flux-model-two-way-binding-in-one-key) wrapper, or `nil` if `value` is not a model.

```luau
local node = Flux.modelNode(props.value)
if node then
	node:set(text)
end
```

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/creation#flux-model-two-way-binding-in-one-key)
]]
function Bind.modelNode(value: unknown): Graph.Node<any>?
	local rawValue: any = value
	return if Bind.isModel(value) then rawValue[2] else nil
end

local pendingChildData: BindData?
local pendingChildValue: any

local function applyPendingChildren()
	local data, value = pendingChildData :: BindData, pendingChildValue
	pendingChildData, pendingChildValue = nil, nil
	applyChildren(data, value)
end

--- @ignore
function Bind.children<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>, parent: Instance, layoutOrder: number?): () -> ()
	local data = getBindData(node)
	bindGeneration += 1
	local token = bindGeneration
	local function disconnectBind()
		local current = data.children
		if current ~= nil and current.token == token then
			cleanupChildrenBind(node, parent)
		end
	end

	local children = data.children
	if children == nil then
		children = { list = {} }
		data.children = children
	else
		if children.cleanupConnection then
			children.cleanupConnection:Disconnect()
		end
		local oldParent = children.parent
		if oldParent ~= nil and oldParent ~= parent then
			for _, child in children.list do
				if child and child.Parent == oldParent then
					child.Parent = nil
				end
			end
			table.clear(children.list)
		end
	end
	children.cleanupConnection = parent.Destroying:Once(disconnectBind)
	children.order = layoutOrder or 1
	children.parent = parent
	children.token = token

	local restart = data.flushed
	if restart then
		data.eff:Destroy()
		data.eff = startBindEffect(node, data)
	end
	if isReactive() then
		pendingChildData, pendingChildValue = data, raw(node)
		untrack(applyPendingChildren)
	else
		applyChildren(data, raw(node))
	end
	if restart and next(data.fn) ~= nil then
		data.eff:peek()
	end
	return disconnectBind
end

--[[
Subscribes `fn` to updates of `node` with [`RBXScriptSignal:Connect`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/datatypes/RBXScriptSignal#Connect) semantics and returns an unsubscribe function.
Fires on each flush after `node` changes, spawning `fn(value)` on its own thread via [`task.spawn`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/libraries/task#spawn) so callbacks may yield freely.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/effects#bridging-to-external-systems)
]]
function Bind.listen<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>, fn: (value: T) -> ()): () -> ()
	if not isNode(node) then
		error(`Flux.listen expects a reactive node, got {compatTypeof(node)}`, 2)
	elseif type(fn) ~= "function" then
		error(`Flux.listen expects a function, got {compatTypeof(fn)}`, 2)
	end
	local data = getBindData(node)
	if not data.flushed then
		data.eff:peek()
	end
	local fnData = data.fn
	fnData[fn] = true
	return function()
		fnData[fn] = nil
	end
end

--- @ignore
function Bind.from<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>, instance: Instance, property: string, isAttribute: boolean?)
	local name, attribute, isTag = resolveKey(property, isAttribute)
	local rawNode: any = node
	local rawInstance: any = instance
	local disconnect: any
	if isTag then
		rawNode:set(instance:HasTag(name))
		disconnect = onTagChanged(instance, name, function(hasTag)
			rawNode:set(hasTag)
		end)
	else
		rawNode:set(if attribute then instance:GetAttribute(name) else rawInstance[name])
		local connection = onChanged(instance, name, attribute, function(value)
			rawNode:set(value)
		end)
		disconnect = function()
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end
	return node, bindDestroy(node, disconnect)
end

local function follow(instance: Instance, property: string): Graph.Node<any>
	return (Bind.from(signal(NO_VALUE), instance, property))
end

-- The `"Name"` singleton in `property`'s type keeps a literal argument from widening to `string`, so `K` stays the key.
--[[
Creates a [node](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/signals) mirroring an [`Instance`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance) property, an attribute (`$Name` or `_attr_Name`), or a [`CollectionService`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/CollectionService) tag (`#Tag` or `_tag_Tag`).
Disconnects automatically when the node or its owning scope is destroyed.

```luau
local text = Flux.property(textBox, "Text")
local health = Flux.property(character, "$Health")
local isEnemy = Flux.property(character, "#Enemy")
```

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/signals#binding-from-an-instance-property)
]]
function Bind.property<I, K>(instance: I & Instance, property: K | "Name"): Graph.Node<Type.PropertyType<I, K>>
	if not isInstance(instance) then
		error(`Flux.property expects an Instance, got {compatTypeof(instance)}`, 2)
	elseif type(property) ~= "string" then
		error(`Flux.property expects a property, "$Attribute", or "#Tag" name, got {compatTypeof(property)}`, 2)
	end
	return follow(instance, property)
end

-- The core constructor behind `Flux(...)`: a value becomes a signal, a function a computed, and an Instance with a
-- property, `"$Attribute"` / `"_attr_Attribute"`, or `"#Tag"` / `"_tag_Tag"` name a `Bind.property` node.
--- @ignore
function Bind.node(obj: any, second: string?): Graph.Node<any>
	if isInstance(obj) then
		if type(second) ~= "string" then
			error(
				`Flux(instance, property) expects a property, "$Attribute", or "#Tag" name, got {compatTypeof(second)}`,
				3
			)
		end
		return follow(obj, second)
	elseif second ~= nil then
		error(`Flux(value) takes a single argument; only an Instance takes a property name`, 3)
	end
	return new(obj)
end

--[[
Wraps `fn` so a [computed](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/computeds) or [effect](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/effects) tracks only `deps` and runs `fn(input, prevInput, prevResult)` untracked.
Pass `defer = true` to skip the initial run and fire only when `deps` change.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/tracking#flux-on)
]]
function Bind.on<D, R>(
	deps: any,
	fn: (input: any, prevInput: any?, prevResult: R?) -> R,
	defer: boolean?
): (prevResult: R?) -> R?
	local isArray = type(deps) == "table" and not isNode(deps)
	local count = if isArray then #(deps :: { any }) else 0
	local prevInput: any = nil
	local curInput: any = nil
	local curPrevResult: any = nil
	local function runOnFn(): R
		local input, prevRes = curInput, curPrevResult
		curInput, curPrevResult = nil, nil
		return fn(input, prevInput, prevRes)
	end

	return function(prevResult: R?): R?
		local input
		if isArray then
			input = table.create(count)
			for i = 1, count do
				input[i] = read(deps[i])
			end
		else
			input = read(deps)
		end

		if defer then
			defer = false
			prevInput = input
			return prevResult
		end

		curInput, curPrevResult = input, prevResult
		local result = untrack(runOnFn)
		prevInput = input
		return result
	end
end

--- @ignore
function Bind.to<T>(node: Graph.Node<T>, instance: Instance, property: string, isAttribute: boolean?)
	local data = getBindData(node)
	local attribute = isAttribute == true
	local index = if attribute then 1 else 2
	release(instance, property, attribute)

	local value = raw(node)
	local function applyInitial()
		if attribute then
			setAttribute(instance, property, value)
		else
			setProperty(instance, property, value)
		end
	end
	if isReactive() or Graph.getOwner() ~= nil then
		withOwner(NO_VALUE, function()
			untrack(applyInitial)
		end)
	else
		applyInitial()
	end

	local binds = data.rbx[instance]
	if binds == nil then
		binds = {}
		data.rbx[instance] = binds
	end
	local bucket = binds[index]
	if bucket == nil then
		bucket = {}
		binds[index] = bucket
	end

	bindGeneration += 1
	local token = bindGeneration
	bucket[property] = token

	local function unbind()
		if bucket[property] ~= token then
			return
		end
		bucket[property] = nil
		if (binds[1] == nil or next(binds[1]) == nil) and (binds[2] == nil or next(binds[2]) == nil) then
			data.rbx[instance] = nil
		end
	end

	local key = claimKey(property, attribute)
	local claim: Claim = { unbind }
	local owned = claims[instance]
	if owned == nil then
		owned = {}
		claims[instance] = owned
	end
	owned[key] = claim

	return function()
		local current = claims[instance]
		if current and current[key] == claim then
			current[key] = nil
			if next(current) == nil then
				claims[instance] = nil
			end
		end
		unbind()
	end
end

--- @ignore
--- Releases the source currently bound to an instance property or attribute, so a static write replaces it.
Bind.release = release

--- @ignore
--- Ties `releaser` (a cleanup function or cleanable) to the current binding of a key, run when a later edit replaces it.
function Bind.attach(instance: Instance, property: string, isAttribute: boolean?, releaser: any)
	local owned = claims[instance]
	local claim = owned and owned[claimKey(property, isAttribute)]
	if claim then
		table.insert(claim, releaser)
	end
end

return table.freeze(Bind)

--!strict
--[[
Shared clock for timers, frame callbacks, and deterministic stepping in tests.
Delegates to `os.clock()`, `workspace:GetServerTimeNow()`, `task.*`, and `RunService` in live games, or steps virtual time in manual mode (`Clock.manual(true)`).

```luau
local Clock = Flux.Clock
Clock.manual(true)
Clock.delay(1, function() print("one second later") end)
Clock.step(1) -- advances 1 second in 1/60s frames
```
]]

local IS_ROBLOX = game ~= nil

export type Phase = "PreRender" | "RenderStepped" | "Heartbeat"

local EPOCH = 1767225600 -- 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
local EPSILON = 1e-9
local DRAIN_LIMIT = 10000

local osClock = os.clock
local engineTask: any = task
local RunService: any = if IS_ROBLOX then game:GetService("RunService") else nil

local manual = not IS_ROBLOX
local virtualNow = 0

--- @ignore
type Timer = {
	due: number,
	seq: number,
	thread: thread,
	start: number?,
	args: { any }?,
	cancelled: boolean?,
}

--- @ignore
type Deferred = {
	thread: thread,
	args: { any }?,
	cancelled: boolean?,
}

local heap: { Timer } = {}
local seq = 0
local timerOf: { [thread]: Timer } = {}

local queue: { Deferred } = {}
local head, tail = 1, 0
local deferredOf: { [thread]: Deferred } = {}

local render: { (dt: number) -> () } = {}
local heartbeat: { (dt: number) -> () } = {}

local frameHook: ((dt: number) -> ())? = nil
local report: (...any) -> () = if IS_ROBLOX then warn else print

local function before(a: Timer, b: Timer): boolean
	return a.due < b.due or (a.due == b.due and a.seq < b.seq)
end

local function push(timer: Timer)
	local index = #heap + 1
	heap[index] = timer
	while index > 1 do
		local parent = index // 2
		if not before(heap[index], heap[parent]) then
			break
		end
		heap[index], heap[parent] = heap[parent], heap[index]
		index = parent
	end
end

local function pop(): Timer
	local top = heap[1]
	local last = table.remove(heap) :: Timer
	local size = #heap
	if size > 0 then
		heap[1] = last
		local index = 1
		while true do
			local left, right, smallest = index * 2, index * 2 + 1, index
			if left <= size and before(heap[left], heap[smallest]) then
				smallest = left
			end
			if right <= size and before(heap[right], heap[smallest]) then
				smallest = right
			end
			if smallest == index then
				break
			end
			heap[index], heap[smallest] = heap[smallest], heap[index]
			index = smallest
		end
	end
	return top
end

local function resume(thread: thread, ...: any)
	if coroutine.status(thread) ~= "suspended" then
		return
	end
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		engineTask.spawn(thread, ...)
		return
	end
	local ok, err = coroutine.resume(thread, ...)
	if not ok then
		report(debug.traceback(thread, `[Flux] Clock: error in a resumed thread: {err}`))
	end
end

local function resumeArgs(thread: thread, args: any)
	if args then
		resume(thread, table.unpack(args, 1, args.n))
	else
		resume(thread)
	end
end

local function toThread(fnOrThread: any): thread
	return if type(fnOrThread) == "thread" then fnOrThread else coroutine.create(fnOrThread)
end

local function scheduleTimer(seconds: number?, thread: thread, start: number?, args: { any }?)
	seq += 1
	local timer: Timer = {
		due = virtualNow + math.max(seconds or 0, 0),
		seq = seq,
		thread = thread,
		start = start,
		args = args,
	}
	timerOf[thread] = timer
	push(timer)
end

local function canWait(): boolean
	if not coroutine.isyieldable() then
		return false
	elseif IS_ROBLOX then
		return true
	end
	local level, bottom = 2, nil
	while true do
		local fn = debug.info(level, "f")
		if fn == nil then
			break
		end
		bottom = fn
		level += 1
	end
	if bottom == nil or debug.info(bottom, "s") == "[C]" then
		return true
	end
	local params, vararg = debug.info(bottom, "a")
	return not (debug.info(bottom, "l") <= 1 and params == 0 and vararg)
end

local Clock = {}

--[[
Seconds on a monotonic clock, for measuring intervals: `os.clock()` in a game, virtual time on a manual clock.
]]
function Clock.now(): number
	return if manual then virtualNow else osClock()
end

--[[
Unix time in seconds, for dates and countdowns shared between players: `workspace:GetServerTimeNow()` in a game,
`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z + now()` on a manual clock.
]]
function Clock.wall(): number
	if manual then
		return EPOCH + virtualNow
	end
	return if IS_ROBLOX then workspace:GetServerTimeNow() else os.time()
end

local function pack(...: any): { any }?
	if select("#", ...) == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local packed: { any } = table.pack(...)
	return packed
end

--[[
Runs `fn(...)` (or resumes a thread) after `seconds`, like `task.delay`. Returns the thread, for `cancel`.
]]
function Clock.delay<A...>(seconds: number?, fn: ((A...) -> ...any) | thread, ...: A...): thread
	if not manual then
		return engineTask.delay(seconds, fn, ...)
	end
	local thread = toThread(fn)
	scheduleTimer(seconds, thread, nil, pack(...))
	return thread
end

--[[
Yields the running thread for `seconds` (default: one frame), like `task.wait`, and returns the time it waited. On a
manual clock it waits for a `step` to pass the deadline, so it needs a coroutine to yield.
]]
function Clock.wait(seconds: number?): number
	if not manual then
		return engineTask.wait(seconds)
	end
	local thread = coroutine.running()
	if not canWait() then
		error("Clock.wait on a manual clock needs a yieldable coroutine; run it in a thread a step can resume", 2)
	end
	scheduleTimer(seconds, thread, virtualNow, nil)
	return coroutine.yield()
end

--[[
Runs `fn(...)` (or resumes a thread) once the current work finishes, like `task.defer`. On a manual clock it waits for
`drain()` (which every `step` frame calls). Returns the thread, for `cancel`.
]]
function Clock.defer<A...>(fn: ((A...) -> ...any) | thread, ...: A...): thread
	if not manual then
		return engineTask.defer(fn, ...)
	end
	local thread = toThread(fn)
	local entry: Deferred = { thread = thread, args = pack(...) }
	deferredOf[thread] = entry
	tail += 1
	queue[tail] = entry
	return thread
end

--[[
Cancels a thread from `delay`, `defer` or a `wait`, like `task.cancel`.
]]
function Clock.cancel(thread: thread)
	if not manual then
		engineTask.cancel(thread)
		return
	end
	local timer = timerOf[thread]
	if timer then
		timer.cancelled = true
		timer.args = nil
		timerOf[thread] = nil
	end
	local entry = deferredOf[thread]
	if entry then
		entry.cancelled = true
		entry.args = nil
		deferredOf[thread] = nil
	end
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		engineTask.cancel(thread)
	elseif coroutine.status(thread) == "suspended" then
		coroutine.close(thread)
	end
end

--[[
Calls `fn(dt)` every frame at `phase` ("PreRender", "RenderStepped" or "Heartbeat"). Returns a function that
disconnects it. A manual clock calls it from `step` instead of the engine's frames.
]]
function Clock.connect(phase: Phase, fn: (dt: number) -> ()): () -> ()
	local list = if phase == "Heartbeat"
		then heartbeat
		elseif phase == "PreRender" or phase == "RenderStepped" then render
		else error(`Clock.connect: unknown phase "{phase}" (PreRender, RenderStepped or Heartbeat)`, 2)
	if not manual then
		local connection = RunService[phase]:Connect(fn)
		return function()
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end
	local entry = function(dt: number)
		fn(dt)
	end
	table.insert(list, entry)
	return function()
		local index = table.find(list, entry)
		if index then
			table.remove(list, index)
		end
	end
end

--[[
Toggles manual clock mode for tests (headless Luau is always manual).
Disabling manual mode clears pending tasks via `Clock.reset()`.
]]
function Clock.manual(on: boolean)
	if not IS_ROBLOX or on == manual then
		return
	end
	if on then
		virtualNow = math.max(virtualNow, osClock())
		manual = true
	else
		Clock.reset()
		manual = false
	end
end

--[[
Tests only: whether the clock is manual.
]]
function Clock.isManual(): boolean
	return manual
end

--[[
Tests only: runs deferred work until none is left, including work it defers in turn. Errors after 10000 calls, when
deferred work keeps deferring more.
]]
function Clock.drain()
	local count = 0
	while head <= tail do
		count += 1
		if count > DRAIN_LIMIT then
			table.clear(queue)
			table.clear(deferredOf)
			head, tail = 1, 0
			error(`Clock.drain: deferred work did not settle after {DRAIN_LIMIT} calls`, 2)
		end
		local entry = queue[head]
		queue[head] = nil
		head += 1
		if not entry.cancelled then
			if deferredOf[entry.thread] == entry then
				deferredOf[entry.thread] = nil
			end
			resumeArgs(entry.thread, entry.args)
		end
	end
	head, tail = 1, 0
end

local function runFrame(dt: number)
	local last = seq
	while heap[1] ~= nil and heap[1].due <= virtualNow + EPSILON and heap[1].seq <= last do
		local timer = pop()
		if not timer.cancelled then
			if timerOf[timer.thread] == timer then
				timerOf[timer.thread] = nil
			end
			if timer.start then
				resume(timer.thread, virtualNow - timer.start)
			else
				resumeArgs(timer.thread, timer.args)
			end
		end
	end
	Clock.drain()
	if #render > 0 then
		for _, subscriber in table.clone(render) do
			subscriber(dt)
		end
		Clock.drain()
	end
	if frameHook then
		frameHook(dt)
		Clock.drain()
	end
	if #heartbeat > 0 then
		for _, subscriber in table.clone(heartbeat) do
			subscriber(dt)
		end
		Clock.drain()
	end
end

--[[
Tests only: advances a manual clock by `seconds`, in frames of at most `frameLength` seconds (default 1/60). `step(0)`
runs one frame of zero length: due timers, subscribers, a Flux step and the deferred work.
]]
function Clock.step(seconds: number, frameLength: number?)
	if not manual then
		error("Clock.step needs a manual clock; call Clock.manual(true) first", 2)
	end
	local length = frameLength or 1 / 60
	assert(seconds >= 0, "Clock.step: seconds must not be negative")
	assert(length > 0, "Clock.step: the frame length must be positive")
	local start = virtualNow
	local frames = math.max(math.ceil(seconds / length - EPSILON), 1)
	for index = 1, frames do
		local target = if index == frames then start + seconds else start + index * length
		local dt = target - virtualNow
		virtualNow = target
		runFrame(dt)
	end
end

--[[
Tests only: drops every pending timer, `wait`, deferred call and manual subscriber. `now` keeps its value.
]]
function Clock.reset()
	table.clear(heap)
	table.clear(timerOf)
	table.clear(queue)
	table.clear(deferredOf)
	head, tail = 1, 0
	table.clear(render)
	table.clear(heartbeat)
end

-- Internal, not part of `Flux.Clock`: init.luau installs the Flux frame step, Compat routes errors through its `warn`
-- and runs its headless `task.spawn` through `resume`.
--- @ignore
Clock._internal = table.freeze({
	setFrame = function(fn: ((dt: number) -> ())?)
		frameHook = fn
	end,
	setReport = function(fn: (message: string) -> ())
		report = fn
	end,
	spawn = function(fnOrThread: any, ...: any): thread
		local thread = toThread(fnOrThread)
		resume(thread, ...)
		return thread
	end,
})

return table.freeze(Clock)

--!strict
local Clock = require("./Clock")

local IS_ROBLOX = game ~= nil
if not IS_ROBLOX then
	(require :: any)("@sert").doubles.Datatypes.installGlobals()

type Task = {

}

type Compat = {
	isRoblox: boolean,
	traceback: (err: any, level: number?) -> any,
	warn: (...any) -> (),
	setWarnHook: (hook: ((message: string) -> ())?) -> (),

local rawWarn: (...any) -> () = if IS_ROBLOX then warn else print

	local hook = warnHook
	if hook then
		local parts: any = table.pack(...)
		for i = 1, parts.n do
			parts[i] = tostring(parts[i])
		end
		hook(table.concat(parts, " ", 1, parts.n))

	end
	rawWarn(...)

local function setWarnHook(hook: ((message: string) -> ())?)
	warnHook = hook
end

local function traceback(err: any, level: number?): any
	return if type(err) == "string" then debug.traceback(err, level) else err

Clock._internal.setReport(warn)

local compatTask: any = table.freeze({

	defer = Clock.defer,
	delay = Clock.delay,
	wait = Clock.wait,
	cancel = Clock.cancel,
})

local Compat: any = {

	warn = warn,
	setWarnHook = setWarnHook,
	task = compatTask,
	clock = Clock.now,
	typeof = typeof,
	services = if IS_ROBLOX
		then setmetatable({}, {

				local service = (game.GetService :: any)(game, name)
				self[name] = service

			end,

		else {} :: { [string]: any },
	Instance = if IS_ROBLOX then Instance else nil,
	Color3 = Color3,
	UDim = UDim,
	UDim2 = UDim2,
	Vector2 = Vector2,
	Vector3 = Vector3,
	CFrame = CFrame,
	Rect = Rect,
	NumberRange = NumberRange,
	Font = Font,
	TweenInfo = TweenInfo,
	Enum = Enum,
	ColorSequence = ColorSequence,
	ColorSequenceKeypoint = ColorSequenceKeypoint,

if IS_ROBLOX then

--!strict
--[[
Control flow, list mapping, and keyed selection helpers (`show`, `showKeyed`, `switch`, `presence`, `pick`, `fallback`, `forValue`, `forIndex`, `selector`).

```luau
Flux.show(loggedIn, function() return Profile {} end, function() return SignIn {} end)
```
]]

local Compat = require("./Compat")
local Graph = require("./Graph")

local warn = Compat.warn
local computed = Graph.computed
local dispose = Graph.dispose
local effect = Graph.effect
local newValue = Graph.signal
local raw = Graph.raw
local read = Graph.read
local get = Graph.Node.get
local set = Graph.Node.set
local destroyNode = Graph.Node.Destroy
local untrack = Graph.untrack
local retrack = Graph.retrack
local scope = Graph.scope
local withOwner = Graph.withOwner
local isReactive = Graph.isReactive
local isStale = Graph.isStale
local isObserved = Graph.isObserved

--- @ignore
type Node<T> = Graph.Node<T>
--- @ignore
type Item<L> = index<Graph.Unwrap<L>, number>

--- @ignore
type function NonNil(t: type): type
	if t:is("nil") then
		return types.never
	elseif not t:is("union") then
		return t
	end
	local parts = {}
	for _, part in t:components() do
		if not part:is("nil") then
			table.insert(parts, part)
		end
	end
	return if #parts == 0 then types.never elseif #parts == 1 then parts[1] else types.unionof(table.unpack(parts))
end

local OTHERWISE: any = table.freeze({ type = "SwitchOtherwise" })
local UNSET = table.freeze({})
local NO_VALUE: any = nil

-- Conditional (show, showKeyed, switch, presence, pick, fallback) -----------------------------------------------------

local function bindLifetime(output: Node<any>)
	if Graph.getOwner() ~= nil then
		Graph.cleanup(output)
	end
end

local function mountBranch(fn: any, a: any, b: any): (boolean, any, any)
	local ok, branch, result = pcall(withOwner, NO_VALUE, function()
		return scope(function(): any
			return fn(a, b)
		end)
	end)
	if ok then
		return true, branch, result
	end
	return false, branch, nil
end

local function mount(
	source: any,
	selectBranch: (value: any, a: any, b: any, c: any) -> (any, ((value: () -> any) -> any)?),
	argA: any,
	argB: any,
	argC: any
): Node<any>
	local activeKey: any = UNSET
	local activeBranch: Node<any>? = nil
	local output = newValue(NO_VALUE)

	local function valueOf()
		local current = read(source)
		return current
	end

	local driver = effect(function()
		local value = read(source)
		local key, factory = selectBranch(value, argA, argB, argC)

		if key == activeKey then
			return
		end
		activeKey = key

		untrack()
		local previous = activeBranch
		activeBranch = nil
		if previous ~= nil then
			previous:Destroy()
		end

		if factory ~= nil then
			local ok, branch, result = mountBranch(factory, valueOf)
			if ok then
				activeBranch = branch
				set(output, result)
			else
				set(output, nil)
				activeKey = UNSET
				retrack()
				error(branch, 0)
			end
		else
			set(output, nil)
		end
		retrack()
	end)

	output:onDestroy(function()
		driver:Destroy()
		local branch = activeBranch
		activeBranch = nil
		if branch ~= nil then
			branch:Destroy()
		end
	end)
	bindLifetime(output)

	return output
end

local function showSelect(value: any, component: any, fallback: any, keyed: any): (any, any)
	local factory = if value then component else fallback
	return (if keyed then value else not not value), factory
end

local function switchSelect(value: any, map: { [any]: any }): (any, any)
	local factory = map[value]
	if factory == nil then
		local otherwise = map[OTHERWISE]
		if otherwise ~= nil then
			return OTHERWISE, otherwise
		end
	end
	return value, factory
end

local function show<T, F>(
	condition: unknown,
	component: (value: () -> any) -> T,
	fallback: ((value: () -> any) -> F)?
): Node<T | F>
	return mount(condition, showSelect, component, fallback, false)
end

local function showKeyed<T, F>(
	condition: unknown,
	component: (value: () -> any) -> T,
	fallback: ((value: () -> any) -> F)?
): Node<T | F>
	return mount(condition, showSelect, component, fallback, true)
end

--[[
Mounts the branch factory matching `source`'s current value in its own child [scope](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/scopes).
Use `[Flux.otherwise]` in `map` as a catch-all branch for unmatched values.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#switching-between-many-branches)
]]
local function switch<S>(source: S)
	return function<T>(map: { [Graph.Unwrap<S>]: (value: () -> Graph.Unwrap<S>) -> T }): Node<T?>
		local mounted: any = mount(source, switchSelect, map, nil, nil)
		return mounted
	end
end

--[[
Mounts `component(exiting, done)` while `condition` is truthy and keeps it mounted while `exiting()` is `true` until `done()` is called.
If `condition` turns truthy again before `done()` runs, `exiting` flips back to `false` without remounting.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#animating-exits-with-presence)
]]
local function presence<T>(condition: unknown, component: (exiting: Node<boolean>, done: () -> ()) -> T): Node<T?>
	local output: any = newValue(NO_VALUE)
	local branch: Node<any>? = nil
	local exiting: Node<boolean>? = nil
	local finished = newValue(0)
	local handled = 0

	local function done()
		local leaving = exiting
		if leaving ~= nil and leaving:peek() then
			set(finished, finished:peek() + 1)
		end
	end

	local driver = effect(function()
		local present = read(condition)
		local finishes = get(finished)

		untrack()
		local current, leaving = branch, exiting
		if present then
			handled = finishes
			if current == nil then
				local exit = newValue(false)
				local ok, mounted, result = mountBranch(component, exit, done)
				if not ok then
					destroyNode(exit)
					set(output, nil)
					retrack()
					error(mounted, 0)
				end
				branch, exiting = mounted, exit
				set(output, result)
			elseif leaving ~= nil and leaving:peek() then
				set(leaving, false)
			end
		elseif current ~= nil and leaving ~= nil then
			if not leaving:peek() then
				handled = finishes
				set(leaving, true)
			elseif finishes ~= handled then
				branch, exiting = nil, nil
				current:Destroy()
				destroyNode(leaving)
				set(output, nil)
			end
		end
		retrack()
	end)

	output:onDestroy(function()
		driver:Destroy()
		local current, leaving = branch, exiting
		branch, exiting = nil, nil
		if leaving ~= nil then
			destroyNode(leaving)
		end
		destroyNode(finished)
		if current ~= nil then
			current:Destroy()
		end
	end)
	bindLifetime(output)

	return output
end

--[[
Derives a [node](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/signals) returning `whenTrue` while `condition` is truthy and `whenFalse` otherwise.
Only the active branch is read, and no branch scope is created.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#picking-between-values)
]]
local pick = function(condition: unknown, whenTrue: any, whenFalse: any?): Node<any>
	return computed(function(): any
		return if read(condition) then read(whenTrue) else read(whenFalse)
	end)
end :: (<A, B>(condition: unknown, whenTrue: A, whenFalse: B) -> Node<Graph.Unwrap<A> | Graph.Unwrap<B>>) & (<A>(condition: unknown, whenTrue: A) -> Node<Graph.Unwrap<A>?>)

--[[
Derives a [node](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/signals) returning `value` when non-`nil`, or `default` when `value` is `nil`.
Preserves `false` instead of replacing it like `or`.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#defaulting-a-nil-value)
]]
local function fallback<V, D>(value: V, default: D): Node<NonNil<Graph.Unwrap<V>> | Graph.Unwrap<D>>
	return computed(function(): any
		local current = read(value)
		return if current == nil then read(default) else current
	end)
end

-- For (forIndex, forValue) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function createMapper(list: any, mapFn: any, keyedByValue: boolean): Node<any>
	local cache: { [any]: any } = {}
	local nodes: { [any]: Node<any> } = {}
	local currentKeys: { [any]: boolean } = {}
	local cacheN = 0
	local rebuildAborted = false
	local rowA: any, rowB: any

	local function build()
		local a, b = rowA, rowB
		rowA, rowB = nil, nil
		return mapFn(a, b)
	end

	local self = computed(function()
		local current = read(list) :: { any }
		if type(current) ~= "table" then
			return {}
		end

		table.clear(currentKeys)
		local out = table.create(#current)

		local mustScan = rebuildAborted
		rebuildAborted = true
		untrack()

		local seen, added = 0, 0
		for index, value in current do
			local key: any, held: any = index, value
			if keyedByValue then
				key, held = value, index
				if currentKeys[key] ~= nil then
					warn(
						"[Flux] Flux.forValue: duplicate values share one mapped instance (the value is the cache key); use Flux.forIndex"
					)
					seen -= 1
				end
			end
			currentKeys[key] = true
			seen += 1
			local node = nodes[key]
			if node ~= nil then
				set(node, held)
				out[index] = cache[key]
			else
				node = newValue(held)
				if keyedByValue then
					rowA, rowB = node, value
				else
					rowA, rowB = index, node
				end
				local mapped = withOwner(node, build)
				cache[key] = mapped
				nodes[key] = node
				added += 1
				out[index] = mapped
			end
		end

		rebuildAborted = false

		if mustScan or seen ~= cacheN + added then
			local liveN = 0
			for key, node in nodes do
				if currentKeys[key] == nil then
					node:Destroy()
					nodes[key] = nil
					dispose(cache[key])
					cache[key] = nil
				else
					liveN += 1
				end
			end
			cacheN = liveN
		else
			cacheN += added
		end

		return out
	end)

	self:onDestroy(function()
		for key, node in nodes do
			node:Destroy()
			dispose(cache[key])
		end
		table.clear(nodes)
		table.clear(cache)
		table.clear(currentKeys)
	end)

	return self
end

--[[
Maps `list` by numeric index, running `mapFn(index, item)` once per slot and updating `item` in place when the value at that index changes.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/mapping#flux-forindex-keyed-by-index)
]]
local function forIndex<L, U>(list: L, mapFn: (index: number, item: Node<Item<L>>) -> U): Node<{ U }>
	return createMapper(list, mapFn, false)
end

--[[
Maps `list` by item identity, running `mapFn(index, value)` once per unique value and updating `index` when an item moves.
Values must be unique (use `Flux.forIndex` for primitive or duplicate values).

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/mapping#flux-forvalue-keyed-by-value)
]]
local function forValue<L, U>(list: L, mapFn: (index: Node<number>, value: Item<L>) -> U): Node<{ U }>
	return createMapper(list, mapFn, true)
end

-- Selector ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local SWEEP_MIN = 32
local SWEEP_REQUESTED = math.huge

-- A selector: `selector(key)` or `selector:get(key)` reads whether `key` is selected.
export type Selector<K> = setmetatable<{
	--[[
	Reactively reads whether `key` matches the selector's source.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/selectors#reading-a-selection)
	]]
	get: (self: any, key: K) -> boolean,
	--[[
	Destroys the selector and disposes its internal watcher and per-key nodes.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/selectors#cleaning-up)
	]]
	Destroy: (self: any) -> (),
}, { __call: (self: any, key: K) -> boolean }>

--- @ignore
type SelectorData = {
	_nodes: { [any]: Graph.Node<boolean> },
	_count: number,
	_sweepAt: number,
	_watcher: Graph.Node<any>,
	_sweepSignal: Graph.State<boolean>,
	_equals: ((sourceValue: any, key: any) -> boolean)?,
	_active: any,
}

--- @class Selector
local SelectorMT = {}
SelectorMT.__index = SelectorMT

local function sweep(self: SelectorData)
	local nodes = self._nodes
	local count = 0
	for key, node in nodes do
		if isObserved(node) then
			count += 1
		else
			nodes[key] = nil
			destroyNode(node)
		end
	end
	self._count = count
	self._sweepAt = math.max(SWEEP_MIN, 2 * count)
end

--[[
Reactively reads whether `key` matches the selector's source.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/selectors#reading-a-selection)
]]
function SelectorMT.get(self: SelectorData, key: any): boolean
	if isStale(self._watcher) then
		raw(self._watcher)
	end
	local nodes = self._nodes
	local node = nodes[key]
	if node ~= nil then
		return get(node :: Graph.Node<boolean>)
	end

	local equals = self._equals
	local selected = if equals ~= nil then equals(self._active, key) else self._active == key
	if not isReactive() then
		return selected
	end

	if self._count >= self._sweepAt then
		self._sweepAt = SWEEP_REQUESTED
		set(self._sweepSignal, true, true)
	end
	node = newValue(selected)
	nodes[key] = node
	self._count += 1
	return get(node)
end

SelectorMT.__call = SelectorMT.get

--[[
Destroys the selector and disposes its internal watcher and per-key nodes.

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/selectors#cleaning-up)
]]
function SelectorMT.Destroy(self: SelectorData)
	if self._watcher ~= nil then
		self._watcher:Destroy()
	end
end

--[[
Creates a keyed selector that tracks which key matches `source` in O(1) (or O(observed keys) with a custom `equals` comparator).

[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/selectors#creating-a-selector)
]]
local function selector<S, K>(source: S, equals: ((sourceValue: Graph.Unwrap<S>, key: K) -> boolean)?): Selector<K>
	local sweepSignal = newValue(false)
	local nodes: { [any]: Graph.Node<boolean> } = {}
	local self: any = setmetatable({
		_nodes = nodes,
		_count = 0,
		_sweepAt = SWEEP_MIN,
		_equals = equals,
		_active = UNSET,
		_watcher = NO_VALUE,
		_sweepSignal = sweepSignal,
	}, SelectorMT)

	self._watcher = effect(function()
		local value = read(source)
		local prev = self._active
		if equals == nil and prev == value then
			return
		end
		self._active = value
		if self._count == 0 then
			return
		end

		untrack()
		if equals == nil then
			local prevNode = if prev ~= nil then nodes[prev] else nil
			if prevNode ~= nil then
				set(prevNode, false)
			end
			local nextNode = if value ~= nil then nodes[value] else nil
			if nextNode ~= nil then
				set(nextNode, true)
			end
		else
			for key, node in nodes do
				set(node, equals(value, key))
			end
		end
		retrack()
	end)

	local sweeper = effect(function()
		get(sweepSignal)
		if self._sweepAt == SWEEP_REQUESTED then
			sweep(self)
		end
	end)

	self._watcher:onDestroy(function()
		for _, node in nodes do
			destroyNode(node)
		end
		sweeper:Destroy()
		destroyNode(sweepSignal)
		table.clear(self)
	end)

	return self
end

return table.freeze({
	--[[
	Catch-all branch key for [`Flux.switch`](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#a-catch-all-branch) maps when `source` matches no explicit key.

	```luau
	Flux.switch(state) {
		loading = function() return Spinner {} end,
		[Flux.otherwise] = function(value) return Label { text = value } end,
	}
	```

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#a-catch-all-branch)
	]]
	otherwise = OTHERWISE,
	--[[
	Mounts `component` while `condition` is truthy, or `fallback` when falsy, in its own child [scope](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/scopes).
	Rebuilds only when truthiness flips (use [`Flux.showKeyed`](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#keyed-show) to rebuild on every identity change).

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#showing-one-of-two-branches)
	]]
	show = show :: (<T>(condition: unknown, component: (value: () -> any) -> T) -> Node<T?>) & (<T, F>(
		condition: unknown,
		component: (value: () -> any) -> T,
		fallback: (value: () -> any) -> F
	) -> Node<(T | F)?>),
	--[[
	Mounts `component` while `condition` is truthy (or `fallback` when falsy) and remounts in a fresh [scope](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/scopes) whenever `condition` changes identity.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/concepts/conditionals#keyed-show)
	]]
	showKeyed = showKeyed :: (<T>(condition: unknown, component: (value: () -> any) -> T) -> Node<T?>) & (<T, F>(
		condition: unknown,
		component: (value: () -> any) -> T,
		fallback: (value: () -> any) -> F
	) -> Node<(T | F)?>),
	switch = switch,
	presence = presence,
	pick = pick,
	fallback = fallback,
	forIndex = forIndex,
	forValue = forValue,
	selector = selector,
})

-- Find ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local FIND_SYMBOL: any = table.freeze({ type = "Symbol" })
local rawGame: any = game

local function indexParent(instance: Instance): Instance?
	return instance.Parent
end

local function queryFirst(instance: Instance, query: string): Instance?
	return instance:QueryDescendants(query)[1]
end

local function findPath(instance: Instance, pathStr: string): Instance?
	local cur: Instance = instance
	for _, segment in string.split(pathStr, ".") do
		if segment == "" then
			continue
		end
		local nextInst = if segment == "Parent" or segment == "^" then cur.Parent else cur:FindFirstChild(segment)
		if not nextInst then
			return nil
		end
		cur = nextInst
	end
	return cur
end

local function makeSelector(find: any): any
	local fn = if type(find) ~= "string"
		then find
		elseif IS_ROBLOX then rawGame[find]
		else function(instance: any, query: string): any
			return instance[find](instance, query)
		end
	return function(query: string)
		return function(properties: Type.Map<any>)
			return { FIND_SYMBOL, fn, properties, query }
		end
	end
end

--- @ignore
type Fallback<Name> = index<Type.Editable & { [string]: Instance }, Name>

export type Selection = { any }
export type ClassSelector = <T>(className: T | keyof<Type.Editable>) -> (Type.EditProperties<Fallback<T>>) -> Selection
-- A name, path or query says nothing about the class it finds, so its property table is untyped.
export type QuerySelector = (query: string) -> (Type.Map<any>) -> Selection
export type ParentSelector = () -> (Type.Map<any>) -> Selection

local function warnFind(query: string?, value: any)
	local desc = if query == nil then "a Find selector" else `query "{query}"`
	warn(`[Flux] Instance expected for {desc}, got {compatTypeof(value)}`)
end

local function resolveFind(
	applied: { any },
	instance: Instance,
	applyProps: (Instance, Type.Map<any>, ...any) -> ...any
)
	local query = applied[4]
	local result = applied[2](instance, query)
	local properties = applied[3]
	local kind = kindOf(result)

	if kind == "Instance" then
		applyProps(result, properties)
	elseif kind == "table" then
		for _, item in result do
			if kindOf(item) == "Instance" then
				applyProps(item, properties)
			else
				warnFind(query, item)
			end
		end
	else
		warnFind(query, result)
	end
end

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	Child = makeSelector("FindFirstChild") :: QuerySelector,
	--[[
	Selects the first direct child of class `className` via
	[`Instance:FindFirstChildOfClass`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance#FindFirstChildOfClass)
	and applies the property table to it.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#available-selectors)
	]]
	ChildClass = makeSelector("FindFirstChildOfClass") :: ClassSelector,
	--[[
	Selects the first direct child matching `IsA(className)` via
	[`Instance:FindFirstChildWhichIsA`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance#FindFirstChildWhichIsA)
	and applies the property table to it.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#available-selectors)
	]]
	ChildIsA = makeSelector("FindFirstChildWhichIsA") :: ClassSelector,
	--[[
	Selects the first descendant named `name` via `Instance:FindFirstChild(name, true)` and applies the property
	table to it.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	Descendant = makeSelector(function(instance: Instance, name: string): Instance?
		return instance:FindFirstChild(name, true)
	end) :: QuerySelector,
	--[[
	Selects the target's [`Instance.Parent`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance#Parent)
	and applies the property table to it (`Find.Parent() { ... }`).

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	Parent = makeSelector(indexParent) :: ParentSelector,
	--[[
	Walks a `.`-separated child path from the target (`Parent` or `^` climbs to `Instance.Parent`) and applies the
	property table to the final [`Instance`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance).

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	Path = makeSelector(findPath) :: QuerySelector,
	--[[
	Selects every descendant matching a Roblox query string via
	[`Instance:QueryDescendants`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance#QueryDescendants)
	and applies the property table to each match.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	Query = makeSelector("QueryDescendants") :: QuerySelector,
	--[[
	Selects the first descendant matching a Roblox query string via
	[`Instance:QueryDescendants`](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Instance#QueryDescendants)
	and applies the property table to it.

	[Open Documentation](https://flux.kohl.gg/guide/roblox/hydration#instance-selectors-flux-find)
	]]
	QueryFirst = makeSelector(queryFirst) :: QuerySelector,
})
